This could have been completed individually with minimal effort! Making it a group project actually increases the workload!

Half of my group members were very competent and we completed the research and slide preparation two weeks before the presentation date. Workload for the group project was very light. This was achieved despite having 3 group members out of 6 being free-riders and contributed minimally.

The weekly discussion did not require much effort. Simply write a response based on the discussion topics posted on canvas every week. I could finish it within half an hour and even respond to my friend's responses.

We just had our integrated test today. We were required to write an essay response to a question posted on canvas. It was easy; simply read through all slides and reading materials a night before and you'll do fine.

sections.teaching: Mark is a great speaker and he can grasp everybody's attention with his Canadian accent. When you get into the classroom, you would probably be entranced by his voice and he could make those boring ethical issues interesting in his lectures.
sections.grading:
To be honest, the grading is not that transparent for this course since I only received the marks of my Progress Report...

Participation (40%):
It includes online discussion, in-class discussion and class attendance as well. Please make sure you do not skip any of the classes as missing one of them would cost you 2% of the final grade. From my point of view, it's worthwhile to spend the 2-hour time with Mark in class (despite of taking the attendance) as he lectures well and speaks fluent and clear english which you would rarely encounter in UST's courses.

And you should be voicing out your opinion at least once per week towards a particular topic in the online discussion. Try not to skip the online discussion cuz Mark would really read the discussion board and jot down everyone's name!

AESP Project (40%)
You have to find a small shop in HK and help facilitate their business growth. Try not to be that ambitious as you only have limited time and manpower.

Final Exam (20%)
A open-book final exam with essay questions only. The whole final exam would be based on the weekly assigned readings. You will be fine if you  can skim through them before you sit for the exam and at least understand what those theories are talking about. Need not to pressurize yourself cuz it's an open-book exam and probably everyone would receive similar score.

Participation: 40%
(a) Online Discussion Forum -  20%
(b) In-class Participation - 20%
AESP Project: 40%
- Progress Report
- Presentation ( assign 1/2 groupmates to present)
- Final Report
Final Exam: 20%

I attended all the lectures and spoke in class once for the every other week (it's a rough estimate, cuz I only speak if I have something to say and purely based on my mood haha).
For the online discussion, I commented on the discussion board almost every week and probably I've missed 2-3 times due to procrastination :(
I also did the presentation with my other groupmate, but it's purely optional since Mark said that the whole group would receive the same grade for presentation.

Final grade: A-
*I could probably score higher if I could type in the discussion board every week and speak more in class; lamentably, I am an introvert :(
The grading is totally non-transparent as mentioned. Just do your best and God will do the rest.

At the same time, you should be typing on the discussion board every week (I think it's not a good idea to skip it because Mark would really read it every week and jot down your names), not to mention those weekly assigned readings which would be tested in final exam.

sections.teaching:

He encourages you to actively ask questions and promises you that you would perform well if you do so.

sections.teaching: Mark is a great & wise professor with abundant experience and exposure to the business field. Make sure you pay attention and fully devote to each class, you'll learn A LOT.
sections.grading:
Generally speaking it takes effort to stand out.

IF you would like a A-range, I'd suggest the following:
- Actively raise questions and answer Mark's questions in class (the prerequisite is you paying attention in class firstly, and FINISH every assigned weekly reading - just take 30~45mins before class is Okay)
- Participate to the weekly Canvas discussion (don't miss any), Mark will actually read your postings, don't write too short (too long is not necessary, neither)
- Finish the ethics project with good team effort (hard to say, but a well-coordinated team always stands out more easily)

Tbh, in the situation that everyone has done averagely well in the group project, what helps you stand out is actually the First point above - your genuine interest in the course, in learning. Trust me, Mark can feel that, and he knows that who pays efforts in each class. (there'd be a max. of 5% bonus in final grading for those kids, just to mention)

Simply put, keep a genuine and pure heart in learning.

I got A.

- posting on Canvas discussion board: 20mins

sections.content: Mark's content is quite broad and touches upon a lot of different business ethical issues that are backed up with real-life cases which are actually quite eye-opening and insightful. The content may not seem all that related to each other, each meeting covers a different subject, but at the end of the whole course, during the integrated test, it actually becomes evident that the whole course is sorta kinda related to one another and it really makes us think of what is ethical to us as an individual in this business world.
sections.teaching: Mark loves to talk and he's good at it haha. I find his teaching style quite nice and not boring, but it does require some level of focus to be engaged in a class for a whole 1 hour 50 minutes without using our phone at all and come up with questions and ideas to bring to the discussions he would have. Mark's teaching style may not work for everyone, it may be more suitable for extroverts who like to pitch in and contribute to the class discussion instead of a conventional classroom setting.
sections.grading:
I have to say that the grading is really not that transparent. Everyone sorta has a general idea that to have a good grade you have to participate in the class discussion, post weekly in the online discussion and have a good group project. But there is no real benchmark of what's good until the day you get your grades which may be a real shock to some who didn't get the grade they were expecting.

For reference, I posted every week on the online forum, talked at least once each class, had a pretty good project and we also had a really good presentation at the end. In which I got an A, but idk if this applies to all cases.
sections.workload: Quite okay I think, suitable for a 2 credit course. Just read the readings before class every week (important!), post weekly on the online forum, put some effort into the group project, try to be active in class and lastly the integrated test which is just a short essay of about 1 hr. Not bad. Oh also don't forget to come to class every week and for all the 2 tutorial of your group.

if you are active and willing to participate, or more specifically---LET HIM REMEMBER YOU(He can call your name), then you will be an A range-candidate. And whether you will have A-, A or A+, is depend on your English level. Sort of like LANG.

sections.content: An introductory course to business ethics and morality, with topics like corporate cultures and values, corporate social responsibility, speaking up and crisis management being explained easily by Prof. Maddy. Apart from teachings, you will also have to complete a group project (Applied Ethics Service Project/AESP).
sections.teaching: Prof. Maddy explains concepts of ethics and morality in a succinct matter, where she uses examples of different corporations and individuals to further explain the concepts taught. She requires students to discuss these issues, and also answer her questions in class in order to get participation marks.
sections.grading:
Grading is lenient and not subjective, as she gives high marks to the individual component as well as the AESP project. If your AESP is more creative and meaningful, the higher the chance you will get a high mark in this area. A database will be provided by Prof. Maddy, such that you can search for previous AESP examples for your reference. As for the individual component, good English and mature thinking are required for the essay. Just make sure you adhere to the word limit and stick with the key concepts to get a good grade. Class participation is equally as important, as they contribute to whether you get a good grade or not. Try to answer as many questions as you can in class, or answer the online review questions afterwards.

Mean for AESP: 25.2/30
Mean for individual component: 41.8/50
sections.workload: The workload for this course is fairly light compared to other subjects that I have studied this semester. The project was easily done and was completed quickly with my efficient groupmates. In the AESP, you will have to write a report of several pages, a 2-page progress report, as well as a class presentation of around 12 minutes. The individual component was also easy to complete, as you will only need to write a 300-word essay and a 500-word essay. You will also need to complete several surveys which contribute to your final mark. Although this course has no attendance, I strongly advise you to attend all sessions of this class to attain the class participation mark.

sections.content:
She covered topics such as the Enron scandal, MeToo movement, Mercedes Benz scandal, studies on morality and the ethics of AI and technology. I know some people found the content useless, but personally, I found the class content to be quite interesting. She had guest speakers from Monetary Authority and the ICAC which was quite interesting. Unfortunately the MA speaker session was on the night before a midterm (that I think most of the class had), so the time wasn't very convenient.

I know some people skipped classes, but I would recommend going to class. In lectures there are in-class exercises worth 10% (which is difficult make up for with online participation if you miss it), and you need to know what topics are covered in class to know what to write in your individual essay at the end (which is worth 15%). The reading material uploaded on canvas doesn't cover everything discussed in lectures, and some of it covers topics that weren't discussed in lectures, so you would need to attend lectures to know which topics were covered in class.
sections.teaching:
Maddy is quite engaging in lessons. She likes to keep the atmosphere casual and encourages different opinions. In class she uses powerpoints, videos and games to keep the class interesting.

To record how many times we contribute in her class, she gives us post-it notes to write down our names, which she collects at the end of the lesson, so any contribution you make will definitely be recorded. She also tries to pick people that haven't contributed much to give everyone a fair chance.

Maddy is a nice professor and tries her best to help students. She is very lenient. For the AESP project, she told us that in the event of unforeseen events (e.g. an NGO at the last minute no longer wants to co-operate with us), she would not penalise us for that, and would rather focus on how we overcame the challenge. Even after the deadline, she will encourage us to hand in assignments or finish surveys, but with a penalty of course (if you're late).

In the beginning, I was a little worried about being in her class because I had no idea whether she would be a good professor as she is new to HKUST. However, I am quite happy with my choice.
sections.grading:
The course is graded based on:
Group Project (30%)
- progress report (5%)
- presentation (5%)
- AESP final report (20%)

Individual component (50%)
- individual essay (15%)
- AESP reflection (10%)
- Reflection Surveys (15%)
- In-class exercises (10%)

Participation (20%)
- in class or online participation

In the reflection survey, you need to reflect on your AESP project and your groupmates, so if you have a freerider in your group, or you are a free rider, Maddy/TA will know about it.

I was initially quite worried about my grade as I knew my group didn't do well AESP project. We ended up getting the lowest score in the class. However in the individual component, I scored the highest in the class and ended up with an A. So I'm quite happy with my score.
sections.workload:
The AESP is quite time consuming. In Maddy's class, your AESP group is assigned randomly, so hope that you won't be put with freeriders, otherwise the project will be stressful.

But other than the AESP project, I would say that the workload is pretty low. Compared with other classes, I think our workload was slightly lower. In Paul Forster's class, they had a midterm and had to write an essay in the beginning of the term (I think it was about the ethics of an industry or sth).

sections.content:
MGMT2010 is kind of boring in general. There are three main components of the course: general ethical theories, analyzing modern ethical problems, and the Applied Ethics Service Project (AESP).

In this class, attendance and participation matters a lot as it will be about 20% of your final grade. Hence, if you don't like talking, it may be a very difficult class for you to take.
sections.teaching:
Professor Ho doesn't actually teach too much apart from the general ethical theories as the latter half of the semester will mainly consist of presentation of different groups of the analysis of modern ethical problems.

In general, it really depends on what kind of person you are. If you like talking about social and ethical issues, you will most likely enjoy the class. However, you will find the class very boring if you are anything other than that kind of people.
sections.grading:
The grading is very subjective and does not have a very good standard. For example, in my language course, I have received full marks for essay writings. However, in my personal reflection (20% of your final grade), I only scored adequately in the grammar criteria which was quite odd.

For the AESP project, it is also very subjective as it is based on the professor and TA's opinion of your project considering the fact that there is no model answer like other courses.

Please note the that the grading problem does not have much relation to the instructor but the course itself.
sections.workload:
There are two main assignments - Dirty Money Presentation and AESP.

Both assignments are group project thus has the workload of a group of people. If you have a bad group (like a lot of free riders), it will be like hell, so the workload really depends on what group you get.

Everyone is randomly assigned to groups of 5 and has to do some kind of service project with a recommended time of 8 hours of service per group member (group meetings don't count). Each group is marked based on how creative their service idea is and the impact they made on the community, however, based on what I know most groups faked their impact so the project is kind of pointless.

Lastly, individual work includes 3 reflection surveys (multiple choice) and an essay reflecting on the course.

sections.content: Every class he will distribute a reading material for beforehand reading and in class he will talk about the topics in the corresponding reading. sections.content:

1. What is ethics?
2. What is the use of ethics? / Ethical theories
3. Moral reasoning our our decisions
4. Corporate Values
5. Ethics in Marketing
6. Corporate Social Responsibilities
7. Conflict of interests
8. Bribery
9. Whistle-blowing
10. Technological dilemmas

sections.workload:

Second, the online discussion forum requires you to do weekly discussions. You react to the topic others raised or what others had said. It will take some time if you try to stand out from all the discussions, as your paragraph has to be longer and more inspiring. I really dug through my brain and wrote around 15 lines of words every week. It was a little bit time-consuming for me.

Third, there are readings distributed after every lesson. They are usually around couple pages long and will be used for in-lesson discussion and the integrated test. Frankly speaking I only read them the day before the test but I do feel I could learn more if I read them every week.

sections.content:
Covers many interesting topics, such as trolleyology, peer pressure and decision makings, ethics in value chains, ethics of superheros and much more. His lecture powerpoints do not have much content (usually just photos), so make sure to attend classes to make sure you know what is being taught.

From what I heard, Paul's class is one of the most interesting among other professors, as he uses a lot of examples from comics and movies.
sections.teaching: Paul is extremely interesting. He uses Marvel superheros to bring out ethical concepts. He is also friendly and engaging and tries to remember his students' names. He also shares his personal experiences but makes sure he is on topic and does not go off-track. One lesson was used to play a movie related to business ethics. He also plays a lot of videos in class so make sure class content is interesting. He asks questions quite frequently and invites students to contribute their ideas. He never disagrees with what students say, and guides students to justify their opinions.
sections.grading:
Participation (Attendance, Classroom Discussions): 15%
Ethics Cafe Online Forum: 15%
Integrated Test: 20%
AESP Group Project: 50%, including:
- Progress report: 5%
- Final Presentation: 5%
- Final Report: 40%

Since there are many students in class who answer questions proactively, I thought Paul can't remember people's names and therefore class participation meant nothing. But apparently the TA sits at the very back of the classroom to mark who answered questions.

Ethics forum is EXTREMELY important. I got a friend who skipped most forum and got C range in the end despite doing very well in the AESP project. Need to do forum once per week, and make sure the content is good. Total number of posts needed was 10, so we could skip 2 weeks.

Integrated test covers class content pretty well. Paul uploads practice papers - MAKE SURE you do them. He basically copied and pasted one part of the practice paper to the integrated test, just with slightly different choices. Also remember the writing framework for analysing ethical issues (the framework appears in his notes quite frequently)

Project is VERY important. My group screwed up group presentation, but luckily our reports were at least average. Make sure to take more photos for the "verification" part of the project. And do not choose random services to do - try to choose things that are related to ethics even though it's hard, otherwise in the "ethics part" of the report, you can only "blow water" and it's hard to get high marks.
sections.workload:
AESP project was horribly busy. My group had many free riders and only 1 or 2 people were working constantly. Paul doesn't let people choose their own groups (draw lots), but you can secretly swap lots with someone. But the workload for other professors is similar as all classes have to do AESP Project.

Ethics cafe is done weekly, but Paul does not require long arguments, so the workload for that part is okay. Just make sure not to deadline fight and find better groupmates, and then AESP project should be okay.

sections.content: Content is really boring since it's mostly case studies about business ethics.
sections.teaching: Although the content in itself is hardly worth taking a look at, the professor does an excellent job in teaching a subject that is inherently boring. sections.grading: Group work carries a large weight on your grade so far, most people will end up doing the work last minute and there will be some freeloaders depending on the kind of people you have on the group. However, you can easily get top marks on the final written quiz as long as you make sure to read every week. Attendance and recitation is also going to make a significant part of your grade.  Simply going to class and having the courage to recite, plus making a weekly contribution to the discussion board on Canvas will likely guarantee that you get a decent grade.
sections.workload: Just readings every week, and contribute to the discussion board on Canvas (don't neglect to contribute to the discussion every week as this is can help pull up your grade a lot).

sections.content:

Besides, there are several cases about firms' scandal, such as Well Fargo and Enron, which may also be asked in the test. One week before the test, Paul will upload the past paper and it's more or less the same.

Apart from that, the AESP project is very important!! Basically, your group need to find a shop and do something for it after knowing what is its needs. Your will be assigned in a group randomly, and your group will need to submit progress report, final report.

Online cafe is very important as well, and you should write on any topics or response to others' every week. As I remember, you need to write 10 times, which mean you can only miss 3 weeks.
sections.teaching: Paul is a very good professor, very helpful, very caring. Having conversation with him is very important and he will always ask questions as well. His teaching is very clear and is most likely discussion based but sometimes with video.

For the AESP, groups are assigned at random. However, variance in reports and presentations is not significant. Therefore, handing in the reports on time, and writing enough will lead to a satisfactory score. AESP is not the key to getting a good grade. There is no evaluation session and the instructor would not acknowledge your contribution to the group. Of course, being the group leader of the project will result in a slightly better grade.

Attendance is crucial for Mark's class. Missing one lesson is almost equivalent to 2% of final score. Don't miss lectures and tutorials! Otherwise, it will be nearly impossible to achieve A range. In-class Participation does not really help as Mark would not remember your name unless you are making a really good answer. Students are generally very active in answering questions, therefore, it is very hard to distinguish yourself from the crowd through answering questions. However, participation in the Online Discussion Board is essential for getting even satisfactory grades. You should at least write a passage on the board per week. At least one per week.

Integrated Task is easy and is basic essay-writing. Everybody gets similar grades and does not make much difference in the overall grade. Just be all-rounded and logically correct in your writing.

There is no peer evaluation. You either have to engage other people constantly, or do most of the jobs. Luckily, I had good team mates, so I didn't have to do most of the works.

ii. Discussion
Your attendance and participation is important.
Also, you need to participate in canvas discussion board at least a week.

iii. Test
It's better for you to have all hands out ready, as he allows open book essay writing. Request for it if he doesn't say anything.

sections.grading:
Participation: 30%
Integrated Test: 20%
Project: 50%

Our group's AESP project wasn't done well, we had missed out lots of things, but turns out I got an A in this class. sections.content: Interactive lessons with the professor sharing his "weekly stories", along with theories illustrated by experiences and supported by practical examples. Typical non-technical, MGMT course with a strong focus on the AESP project/students' own involvements, and for my batch there were no midterms/quizzes/finals, hence the focus was not really on the slides content (we didn't have a textbook), but rather your understanding of the concepts brought up and your ability to reflect and share your own insights afterwards.
sections.teaching: Mark is laid-back and funny, good at telling stories that help you understand the course content, and always able to crack a few jokes which makes you feel better about some 1 hour and 50 minutes long 9 am lessons lol overall a chill and pleasant professor who is able to make the course content a bit more interesting than it is supposed to be. One of the more engaging class experiences for business core courses, so no complaints there.
sections.grading:
10% teaching session
10% discussion forum
10% class participation
30% personal reflections
40% AESP project

Not hard to get an A/B range as long as you are willing to put in some efforts and certainly, don't forget to be attentive and proactive in class discussions (we had news sharing every lesson) and the Canvas forum. (Don't be late or miss classes for the sake of impression marks.) No official peer evaluation form to be filled in for the project, but your group mates (allocated by the professor) can still comment on your performance and contributions if they wish by sending emails to the TA - so definitely be a good team-player!
sections.workload: Main focus and priority is, of course, the AESP project, for which you will need to write a Progress Report and Final Report on, as well as a brief 5-10 minutes presentation for. The challenge mainly lies in whether you can find a good SME (mostly local family businesses like restaurants or stores) or social enterprise as the "partner organization" that you will be helping in achieving business goals etc. Site visits can be time consuming depending on what you'd like to do for the business/organization. As for the other parts, not a heavy workload/difficult task as those are mostly about your (regular) participation and a basic understanding of what's been taught in class.

sections.content: Business ethics and the individual? Seems pretty useless. And it might seem like that the professors were forced to teach this course just for the sake of teaching it but Mark does a great job with making it interesting. He constantly updates his PPTs with relevant business world stories and really tries to engage his students.
sections.teaching: Like I said, he's the best teacher I've had so far. Native english skills, pretty cool guy and quite friendly. He divides his class by giving a quick tip to help you adapt to university in the first few minutes, gives another few to encourage students to share some ideas or thoughts on a news article they read out of class. Then he goes on with his PPT slide about no cellphones in class. Then he starts the lecture by talking himself for 30 minutes while forcing you to either 1. discuss with a partner, 2. discuss in a group, 3. discuss in other groups. There will also be quick in class debates.
sections.grading:
The grading was fair to be honest; however, it seems that many of my upperclassmen hated the grading. In the end, it really comes down to how active you are in class and your AESP project. Just don't be shy, don't take out your cell phone, don't chat randomly in class, don't be late and you can get A.

Participation/class marks is very important because it makes you stand out from the other people that sit in the back and chat. Just raise your hand at every opportunity until he gets sick of seeing your hand. Also, aim to share at least 5 news articles that you've read outside of class.

The AESP project contributes to 40% of your grade and thats basically what he looks at the most. It consists of a progress report (1-2 pages, he gives you the format), a presentation (not graded), and a final report. Our group did a half-hearted job on our progress report and scored 50% on it only because we used the wrong template and had to come up with something during class. Our presentation wasn't top notch either; however, it surely was better than the presentations of the other groups. The report was well written (partly because I was the one writing most of it).

There usually is a test/ in class essay near the finals. This year we wrote an essay about in class articles we read, last year it was a MC test. It changes.
sections.workload:
1. Weekly readings and news articles that you should be prepared to discuss in class
2. AESP project presentation + report (this took the most time), while he says that the presentation is not graded, you should aim to do a good job because it will leave him with a good impression.
3. AESP Progress update report

sections.teaching: In class, Mary tried to get people involved with discussions. Normally the same people tend to raise their hands. Personal Reflection: 20%
Answering question regarding your ethical stance on a situation. It's mainly sharing your own personal thoughts. Graded based on your writing style, ethical connections and insight.

sections.workload:
Workload seems to be much less, in comparison to other classes. Didn't have to do readings, instead, you watch movies.

Personal reflection: Can be done in an hour or two, Max word count 500.

AESP Project:
The workload is decent assuming that your group is efficient and plans ahead of time. Thinking of a topic can be tricky but it's important to pick something that your group is truly interested in. I find it hard to be motivated without an interesting topic.
If your progress journal is detailed, when you write your final report you can take stuff from your progress journal and add it to the final report. Makes your life a lot easier.

Also do go to every class. 3% deduction per absent class without medical certificate.

sections.content:
In this course, you learn about ethical concepts (utilitarianism, duty-based ethics, and so on) and many ethical issues in the world today.
The "real" assignments come at the very end of the course: you have to write a report (group project), and an essay.
Besides those, you have to write one post on the discussion board every week. This can be a lot of work if you have other things to do...
sections.teaching: Mark is a great lecturer. He is very interesting and nice. He has a wide perspective and knows a lot of things (really a lot). He tries to involve everyone in the class.
sections.grading: As long as you complete what you have to do, you can get a decent grade. You must not miss the discussion thing, and must not miss the class--it hurts your grade a lot. The group project can be tough if you have bad group mates but would be okay if you have decent group mates.
sections.workload:
The discussion could be a burden if you have a lot of other things to do. If you really want to do this perfectly (i.e. do research and make your points), it would take time.
The group project depends mostly on your group mates as I said. I think as long as you do not do the project at the last minute, it would be alright.
The essay is open-book, so... it's alright.

sections.content: Content in class ranges on a wide spectrum of topics that include but are not limited to psychology, marketing, business fraud, general philosophical principles ( such as utilitarianism, egalitarianism, etc.) Although the class touches an a multitude of ideas, there is consistently a certain amount of depth and time devoted to each topic.
sections.teaching: Teaching was well done. Half of the class was spent with the professor presenting the idea while the other half of the class was spent doing active discussion. All of the concepts and ideas in class were well presented by the professor. That said, if you are the type of student that is not interested in philosophy, psychology or ethics, this class isn't for you. Like any class, even if the professor explains the content well, if the content itself is boring to the individual, one would not enjoy the class.
sections.grading:
Grading:
-Participation(including attendance,
online discussion, teaching session)     :30%
-Integrated test                                      :20%
-AESP(Applied Ethics Service Project)  :50%

The "midterm" is an essay.

A vast majority of your grade will depend on in class participation -- everyone scores roughly a C+,B-, B (with relatively little variation) on the AESP. Therefore, the difference between a C, B and A for the final grade comes down to class participation. If you participate, you will definitely get at least a B for this class. Also, it is important to note that attending class is fundamental -- if you miss a class, 3% of your final grade is deducted.
sections.workload:
The workload falls under three categories:
1. Participate in the online discussions on Canvas
2. Read the readings before coming to class
3. The AESP

The first two take less than an hour each week to complete. The real crux of the workload comes with the 3rd part -- although it is a group project, if you want a half decent grade both individually and collectively on the AESP, you'll have to spent around an hour or two every week/every other week.

sections.content: Things talked about during lessons are quite interesting. The professor will assign one reading for you every week; then during the lesson, you will have sometime to discuss with people sitting around you based on the topics talked about in the readings. Many group discussions are involved, including the teaching session( which you have to be a 'teacher' in another group, explaining the topic assigned to your group and express your views on it.) and the mini debate. All these are kind of interesting and inspiring.
